speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your symptoms, but I need to clarify your gestational age and whether you are currently experiencing heavy bleeding or passing tissue. Also, please describe the nature of your abdominal pain—is it constant or cramping, and does it radiate to your shoulder?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of a prior C-section and the cessation of contractions with the onset of severe pain and bleeding, I am concerned about placenta accreta or uterine rupture. Have you experienced any leakage of fluid from your vagina, and has the baby moved normally or felt different today? REQUEST IMAGES: Transabdominal_and_transvaginal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Rupture. Based on your history of a prior C-section, sudden cessation of contractions, severe abdominal pain, and vaginal bleeding at term, this is a medical emergency. Please go to the emergency room immediately for an emergency Cesarean section.
